NAHHAS:v5p19/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p19/r11.speaker: غيره
NAHHAS:v5p19/r11.claim: Another authority says صرصر means loud in sound.

NAHHAS:v5p19/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p19/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p19/r12.claim: عاتية means that the wind exceeded its ordinary force.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r15.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r15.claim: Qatada derives صرصر from cold, from the root صر.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r15.anchor: و: «الصرصر» يحتمل أن يكون من الصر أي البرد، وهو قول قتادة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r16.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r16.claim: Others derive صرصر from a sound, as if the word imitates the wind's noise.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r16.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون من صر الشيء إذا صوت، فقال قوم: صوت الريح صرصر،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r17.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r17.claim: عاتية means extremely rebellious: the wind defied its keepers and struck ʿAd with force.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r17.anchor: و «العاتية» معناه: الشديدة المخالفة، فكانت الريح عتت على الخزان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r18.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r18.claim: They report that rain and wind normally descend under an angel's measure, except Noah's flood and ʿAd's wind, which God allowed to break out without the keepers' permission.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r18.anchor: وروي عن علي بن أبي طالب وابن عباس أنهما قالا: إنه لم ينزل من السماء قطرة ماء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r19.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p356#2/r19.claim: Tasḵīr means using a thing through power over it.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p208#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p208#2/r6.speaker: قتادة والربيع والسدي والثوري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p208#2/r6.claim: They say the wind was cold and forceful; Qatada adds that it defied them and pierced their hearts.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p208#2/r6.anchor: عاتية} أي: شديدة الهبوب. قال قتادة: عتت عليهم حتى نقبت عن أفئدتهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p208#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p208#2/r7.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p208#2/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak says the wind was cold and transgressed against them without mercy or blessing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p208#2/r7.anchor: صرصر} باردة {عاتية} عتت عليهم بغير رحمة ولا بركة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p208#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p208#2/r8.speaker: علي وغيره
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p208#2/r8.claim: Ali and others say the wind defied its keepers and escaped without restraint.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p208#2/r8.anchor: عتت على الخزنة فخرجت بغير حساب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r16.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r16.claim: Sarsar can mean a fiercely loud wind that makes a sharp repeated sound.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r17.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r17.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r17.claim: Alternatively sarsar means bitterly cold, from sarr; its repeated cold is so intense that it burns.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r17.anchor: وقيل : الباردة من الصر ، كأنها التي كرر فيها البرد وكثر : فهي تحرق لشدة بردها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r18.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r18.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r18.claim: Atiyah describes a fiercely violent wind, using rebellion metaphorically; it also means the wind exceeded control and tore people from every refuge.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r18.anchor: عاتية } شديدة العصف والعتو استعارة . أو عتت على عاد ، فما قدروا على ردها بحيلة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r19.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r19.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r19.claim: Another view says the wind rebelled against its keepers and escaped their control.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p602/r19.anchor: وقيل : عتت على خزانها ، فخرجت بلا كيل ولا وزن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p603/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p603/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p603/r1.claim: A report says God sends each wind and drop of rain in measured amounts, except in Noah's and Aad's times: floodwaters overwhelmed their keepers, and Aad's wind escaped them; it cites 69:11 and 69:6.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p603/r1.anchor: ما أرسل الله سفينة من ريح إلا بمكيال ولا قطرة من مطر إلا بمكيال إلا يوم عاد ويوم نوح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p603/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p603/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p603/r2.claim: The report's language may simply express exceptional intensity and excess.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p603/r2.anchor: ولعلها عبارة عن الشدة والإفراط فيها

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r19.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r19.claim: The Prophet said he was aided by the east wind, while Ad were destroyed by the west wind.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r19.anchor: روى مجاهد عن ابن عباس قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( نصرت بالصبا وأهلكت عاد بالدبور

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r20.speaker: الضحاك والحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r20.claim: They gloss صرصر as a cold wind, from a word for cold.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r20.anchor: أنها الريح الباردة , قاله الضحاك والحسن , مأخوذ من الصر وهو البرد

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r21.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r21.claim: He glosses صرصر as a loud, howling wind.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r23.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r23.claim: عاتية may mean exceeding its limit or a wind that spares nothing and no one.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r23.anchor: المجاوزة لحدها . الثالث : التي لا تبقى ولا ترقب

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r24.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r24.claim: He says the wind rebelled against the people without mercy, or rebelled against its keepers by God's leave.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p75#2/r24.anchor: لأنها عتت على القوم بلا رحمة ولا رأفة , قاله ابن عباس

ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r9.claim: A very great thing can be called ʿāt or ʿātiya; the description of ʿĀd's fierce wind supports this usage for the overwhelming event.
ZAJJAJ:v5p213/r9.anchor: يقال للشيء العظيم عات وعاتية، وكذلك أهلكوا بالطاغية

TABRISI:69:1-10/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:69:1-10/r4.speaker: ابن عباس، قتادة
TABRISI:69:1-10/r4.claim: The wind that destroyed ʿĀd was cold, its sound so fierce that it made teeth chatter.
TABRISI:69:1-10/r4.anchor: أي باردة عن ابن عباس وقتادة كأنه تصطك الأسنان بما يسمع من صوتها

TABRISI:69:1-10/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:69:1-10/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:69:1-10/r5.claim: Another interpretation of ṣarṣar is a violently blowing wind beyond its usual limit.
TABRISI:69:1-10/r5.anchor: الصرصر الشديدة العصوف المتجاوزة لحدها المعروف

TABRISI:69:1-10/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:69:1-10/r6.speaker: الزهري
TABRISI:69:1-10/r6.claim: Al-Zuhrī transmits from Qubayṣa ibn Dhuʾayb that keepers knew each wind's measure and amount, but the wind sent to ʿĀd overflowed their knowledge and God's anger's measure.
TABRISI:69:1-10/r6.anchor: روى الزهري عن قبيصة بن ذؤيب أنه قال ما يخرج من الريح شيء إلا عليها خزان

ASAD-NOTES:69:1/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:69:1/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:69:1/r2.claim: The translation says Thamud and Ad were overtaken by calamity: Thamud by upheaval, Ad by a storm lasting seven nights and eight days, leaving bodies like hollow palm trunks.
ASAD-NOTES:69:1/r2.anchor: Now as for the Thamud - they were destroyed by a violent upheaval [of the earth]

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p449/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p449/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p449/r5.claim: The ‘Ād were destroyed by tempestuous winter winds; ʿātiyah names an uncontrollable wind, paralleling Thamūd’s ṭāghiyah.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p449/r5.anchor: were routed by tempestuous winter winds.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p449/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p449/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p449/r6.claim: Wind ordinarily serves human life, but God transforms it into death and destruction when people rebel.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p449/r6.anchor: when man becomes rebellious, He transforms this docile wind into an instrument of death and destruction.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p254/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p254/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p254/r9.claim: Aad's wind is called ʿātiyah because it defied its keepers, overcame Aad so they could not shelter, or metaphorically because it blew violently.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p254/r9.anchor: عتت على خزانها فخرجت بغير مقدار، أو على عاد فما قدروا على أن يتستروا منها

DURR-FULL:v8p263/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r10.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r10.claim: A single cry extinguished and destroyed Thamud; the violent wind for ʿAd exceeded its bounds until it pierced their hearts.
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r10.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {فأهلكوا بالطاغية} قال: أرسل الله عليهم صيحة واحدة فأهمدتهم

DURR-FULL:v8p263/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r11.claim: Rain and wind are normally measured; during Noah's flood and ʿAd's destruction they overwhelmed their keepers, as the cited verses say.
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: ما أرسل الله شيئا من ريح إلا بمكيال ولا قطرة من مطر إلا بمكيال

DURR-FULL:v8p263/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r12.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r12.claim: ʿAli likewise says rain and wind normally descend by angelic measure, except that Noah's water and ʿAd's wind were released beyond their keepers' control.
DURR-FULL:v8p263/r12.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه قال: لم تنزل قطرة من ماء إلا بمكيال على يدي ملك

STUDYQURAN:69:6/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:6/r1.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:69:6/r1.claim: Ṣarṣar describes either a noisy wind or a wind so cold that it feels as if it burns.
STUDYQURAN:69:6/r1.anchor: Howling translates ṣarṣar, which indicates either a wind that makes a severe noise or a wind so cold that it feels as if it burns (R)

STUDYQURAN:69:6/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:6/r2.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:69:6/r2.claim: Some say the wind pierced through to the people’s hearts.
STUDYQURAN:69:6/r2.anchor: In this context, some say that it pierced through to their hearts (IK)

STUDYQURAN:69:6/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:6/r3.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:69:6/r3.claim: ʿĀtiyah means the wind overwhelmed the people so they could find no cover and was utmost in strength and severity.
STUDYQURAN:69:6/r3.anchor: Raging translates ʿātiyah, which indicates both that it overcame the people in such a manner that they could find no cover and that it was the utmost in strength and severity (R)

STUDYQURAN:69:6/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:6/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:69:6/r4.claim: The ʿĀd wind is also described as howling in 41:16 and 54:19 and as barren in 51:41.
STUDYQURAN:69:6/r4.anchor: The tribe of ʿĀd is also reported to have been destroyed by a howling wind in 41:16 and 54:19 and by the barren wind in 51:41

TAB-FULL:v23p207#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p207#3/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p207#3/r5.claim: Al-Tabari prefers that the calamity was an overpowering cry: the verse names what destroyed Thamud, just as the parallel statement names Aad's destroying wind in 69:6.
TAB-FULL:v23p207#3/r5.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك بالصواب قول من قال: معنى ذلك: فأهلكوا بالصيحة الطاغية

TAB-FULL:v23p209/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p209/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p209/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās describes a deadly cold wind that assailed ʿĀd without mercy or blessing and blew continuously.
TAB-FULL:v23p209/r1.anchor: عن أبيه، عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وأما عاد فأهلكوا بريح صرصر عاتية} [الحاقة: 6] يقول: بريح مهلكة باردة، عتت عليهم بغير رحمة ولا بركة

TAB-FULL:v23p209/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p209/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p209/r2.claim: Qatāda says the wind was cold and so fierce that it pierced their hearts.
TAB-FULL:v23p209/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، {وأما عاد فأهلكوا بريح صرصر عاتية} [الحاقة: 6] والصرصر الباردة عتت عليهم حتى نقبت

TAB-FULL:v23p209/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p209/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p209/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that winds and rain normally had measured allotments, but on Noah’s and ʿĀd’s days water and wind overwhelmed their keepers.
TAB-FULL:v23p209/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: ما أرسل الله من ريح قط إلا بمكيال ولا أنزل قطرة قط إلا بمثقال

TAB-FULL:v23p209/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p209/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
TAB-FULL:v23p209/r4.claim: ʿAlī reports that an angel measured each drop and wind, except in Noah’s flood and ʿĀd’s wind, when they were released beyond the keepers’ control.
TAB-FULL:v23p209/r4.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب، كرم الله وجهه، قال: لم تنزل قطرة من ماء إلا بكيل على يدي ملك

TAB-FULL:v23p209/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p209/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p209/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses ṣarṣar as severe and ʿātiya as overpowering, having rebelled against and overcome them.
TAB-FULL:v23p209/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {بريح صرصر عاتية} [الحاقة: 6] قال: الصرصر: الشديدة، والعاتية: القاهرة

TAB-FULL:v23p211/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p211/r1.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v23p211/r1.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the wind was cold and ʿātiya means it rebelled against them without mercy or blessing.
TAB-FULL:v23p211/r1.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {بريح صرصر} [الحاقة: 6] يعني: باردة {عاتية} [الحاقة: 6] عتت عليهم

TABATABAI:69:6-12/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:6-12/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:6-12/r3.claim: Ṣarṣar is a cold wind blowing with great force; ʿātiya derives from transgression and denotes exceeding obedience and proper bounds.

BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r10.claim: ʿĀd lived in al-Aḥqāf, the sands from Oman toward Ḥaḍramawt and Yemen; they were Arabs of imposing stature, with the tallest a hundred cubits, the shortest sixty, and heads like domes.
BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r10.anchor: وكانت منازلهم بالأحقاف وهي الرمل بين عمان إلى حضر موت واليمن

BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r11.claim: ʿĀd follows Thamūd because of the chronological order, which also progresses from the less to the more deeply misguided.
BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r11.anchor: وتأخيره عن ثمود من تقدمهم زمانا من قبيل الترقي من الضال الشديد

BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r12.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r12.claim: The wind is identified as the west wind on the basis of the Prophetic saying that the east wind brought victory while the west wind destroyed ʿĀd.

BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r13.claim: Ṣarṣar describes a wind with a harsh, loud whistling or squealing sound as it blows.
BURSEVI:v10p100#3/r13.anchor: أي شديدة الصوت لها صرصرة في هبوبها

THALABI:v10p26/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p26/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p26/r1.claim: The violent wind exceeded its appointed measure, rebelled against its keepers, and surpassed what was proper.
THALABI:v10p26/r1.anchor: عتت على خزانها فلم تطعهم وجاوزت المقدار.

THALABI:v10p26/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p26/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v10p26/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that winds and raindrops are sent in measured amounts, except in the days of ʿAd and Noah: Noah's flood overwhelmed the reservoirs and escaped human control.
THALABI:v10p26/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم «ما أرسل الله سبحانه من ريح إلا بمكيال

QASHANI:69:6-8/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:69:6-8/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:69:6-8/r1.claim: Qashani reads ʿĀd as people who transgress the bounds of religious law through heretical permissiveness in divine unity.
QASHANI:69:6-8/r1.anchor: الغالون المجاوزون حد الشرائع بالتزندق والإباحة في التوحيد

QASHANI:69:6-8/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:69:6-8/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:69:6-8/r2.claim: The violent wind signifies sudden egoic desire arising from frozen nature and lack of ardor and love, driving them to ruin.
QASHANI:69:6-8/r2.anchor: هوى النفس البادرة بجمود الطبيعة وعدم حرارة الشوق والعشق العاتية

ELMALILI:69:6-8/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:6-8/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:6-8/r1.claim: Sarsar is a wind that roars with a harsh sound or a very cold storm; Elmalılı renders the destruction as a violent wind and raging storm.
ELMALILI:69:6-8/r1.anchor: Rîh-i sarsar şiddetli sesle gürleyen veya çok soğuk fırtına.

ELMALILI:69:6-8/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:6-8/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:6-8/r2.claim: Atiya means rebellious and forceful, repeatedly overturning its victims with no means to resist or escape.
ELMALILI:69:6-8/r2.anchor: Azgın büker büker atar, redd ü mukavemete ve halâsa çare bulunmaz.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:4/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:4/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:4/r3.claim: For persisting in unbelief, Ad was struck by a devastating storm that lasted seven nights and eight days and laid people out like uprooted palm trunks.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:4/r3.anchor: fırtına Âd kavminin yurdunda yedi gece sekiz gün devam etmiş; sonunda insanları sökülmüş hurma kütükleri gibi yerlere serivermiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:4/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:4/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:4/r4.claim: Ad's magnificent palaces and mansions were razed, and the people vanished.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:4/r4.anchor: Âd kavminin muhteşem sarayları ve köşkleri yerle bir olmuş; böylece yok olup gitmişlerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:4/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:4/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:4/r5.claim: Their fates serve the Muslim community as lessons and as evidence that the power which brought these disasters can also bring about the Resurrection.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:4/r5.anchor: bu felâketleri gerçekleştiren gücün kıyameti de gerçekleştireceğine bir kanıt olarak zikredilmiştir

BURHAN:v3p439/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p439/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p439/r4.claim: عاتية means severe, but its root adds the sense of rebellious excess to the wind’s intensity.
BURHAN:v3p439/r4.anchor: لأن حقيقة عاتية شديدة والعتو أبلغ لأنه شدة فيها تمرد

BURHAN:v4p9/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p9/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p9/r2.claim: Qur'anic winds are plural in mercy contexts and singular in punishment contexts; ʿĀd's destructive wind is a singular example.
BURHAN:v4p9/r2.anchor: وحيث ذكرت في سياق العذاب أتت مفردة كقوله تعالى ﴿ فأرسلنا عليهم ريحا صرصرا في أيام نحسات ﴾ 4 ﴿ فأرسلنا عليهم ريحا وجنودا لم تروها ﴾ 5 ﴿ وأما عاد فأهلكوا بريح صرصر عاتية ﴾

BURHAN:v3p361/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p361/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p361/r4.claim: The source explains that ṣarṣar lacks feminine marking because it is a wind-specific adjective, unlike ʿātiya, which can describe other feminine nouns.
BURHAN:v3p361/r4.anchor: لأن الصرصر وصف مخصوص بالريح لا يوصف به غيرها فأشبه باب حائض ونحوه بخلاف عاتية فإن غير الريح من الأسماء المؤنثة يوصف به

BURHAN:v3p442/r15.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p442/r15.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p442/r15.claim: The wind's “rebellion” is metaphorical, transferring the quality of insolence to the wind.

RUMMANI:v1p87/r3.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p87/r3.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p87/r3.claim: The wind is severe, and ʿātiyah is stronger than severe: its intensity also conveys rebellious excess.
RUMMANI:v1p87/r3.anchor: وقال عز وجل: {بريح صرصر عاتية} حقيقته شديدة , والعتو أبلغ منه لأن العتو شدة فيها تمرد

ZAJJAJ:v5p214/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p214/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p214/r1.claim: The wind was extremely cold; ṣarṣar denotes intense cold, and the source discusses whether the doubled form conveys repetition.
ZAJJAJ:v5p214/r1.anchor: أي بريح شديدة البرد جدا، والصرصر شدة البرد

ZAJJAJ:v5p214/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p214/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p214/r2.claim: Zajjāj compares ṣarṣar with doubled and undoubled Arabic forms: qalqala entails repeated lifting whereas aqalla means lifting, and doubled sound forms such as ṣarṣar or ṣalṣal contrast with ṣar or ṣal.
ZAJJAJ:v5p214/r2.anchor: إلا أن قلقلته رددته أي كررت رفعه، وأقللته رفعته.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p589/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p589/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p589/r5.claim: The doubled form ṣarṣar occurs three times as an epithet of the wind that destroyed ʿAd, including the verse about the violent wind.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p589/r5.anchor: ومعها المضاعف، صرصر، ثلاث مرات، صفة للريح التى أهلكت عاداً

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/f1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/f1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/f1.claim: The Quran uses al-rīḥ for punishment; its sole apparently beneficial occurrence, 10:22, turns into a storm and ends badly.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/f1.anchor: ولم يستعمل الريح في الخير إلا في موطن واحد أعقبها بالشر

ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the paired clauses require parallel causes: saying one people fell through transgression and the other through instrumental wind is unbalanced, since both could be said to fall through transgression. Al-Ālūsī says the issue is parallelism, not event versus substance.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r1.anchor: قول الزمخشري في تضعيف الثاني لعدم الطباق بينها وبين بريح لا أن ذلك لأن أحدهما عين والآخر حدث

ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r5.claim: Ṣarṣar is an adjective describing the wind; its explanation was given earlier in the commentary.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r5.anchor: ومر الكلام في الصرصر فتذكر وهو صفة ريح

ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r6.claim: ʿĀtiya means violently blowing or having rebelled against ʿĀd; the wind pulled them from shelters, so no stratagem saved them. Its rebellion is metaphorical boundary-breaking.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r6.anchor: ﴿ عاتية ﴾ أي شديدة العصف أو عتت على عاد فما قدروا على ردها

ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r7.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r7.claim: ʿAlī reports that water and wind ordinarily came by measured allotment through angels, but Noah’s flood and ʿĀd’s wind were released beyond their keepers; the Ṣaḥīḥayn and others corroborate it.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r7.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن علي بن أبي طالب كرم الله تعالى وجهه أنه قال لم تنزل قطرة إلا بمكيال على يدي ملك إلا يوم نوح

ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī suggests that the wind’s being “rebellious” figuratively conveys its intensity and excess.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r8.anchor: وقد حكى ذلك في الكشاف ثم قال ولعلها عبارة عن الشدة والإفراط فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r9.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r9.claim: Al-Kashf treats the expression as a representative metaphor; when an image conveys its point without recalling the original story, it can function as a metonymy.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r9.anchor: وخرج ذلك في الكشف على الإستعارة التمثيلية ثم قال إن المثل إذا صار بحيث يفهم منه المقصود من دون نظر إلى أصل القصة جاز أن يقال أنه كناية عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r10.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r10.claim: A further analysis allows an emphatic simile: the wind is likened to someone rebelling against obedience.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p40#5/r10.anchor: وجوز أن يكون هناك تشبيه بليغ من العتو وهو الخروج عن الطاعة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p208/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p208/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p208/r1.claim: The wind was overbearing: it disobeyed its keepers, could not be controlled, and exceeded its measure beyond their ability to know how much escaped.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p208/r1.anchor: عتت على خزانها فلم تطعهم ولم يكن لهم عليها سبيل، وجاوزت المقدار فلم يعرفوا كم خرج منها.

BAYDAWI-FULL:69:5-7/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:5-7/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:5-7/r3.claim: Ṣarṣar means a wind of intense sound or intense cold, from roots denoting loudness or cold.
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:5-7/r3.anchor: أي شديدة الصوت أو البرد من الصر أو الصر

BAYDAWI-FULL:69:5-7/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:5-7/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:5-7/r4.claim: The wind was fiercely violent, as though it defied its keepers' control or defied ʿĀd's efforts to repel it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:5-7/r4.anchor: شديدة العصف كأنها عتت على خزانها فلم يستطيعوا ضبطها، أو على { عاد } فلم يقدروا على ردها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r8.claim: ʿĀd are the people of the prophet Hūd.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r9.claim: The ṣarṣar wind combined extreme cold and piercing sound, intensified until the cold burned and the sound deafened.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r9.anchor: أي هي في غاية ما يكون من شدة البرد والصوت كأنه كرر فيها البرد حتى صار يحرق بشدته

BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r10.speaker: الملوي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r10.claim: Al-Malwī says the root ṣarr denotes severe cold or severe heat.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r10.anchor: وقال الملوي : أصله صر وهو البرد الشديد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r11.claim: ʿĀtiyah means beyond bounds in force and destructive gusts; its custodians could not restrain it, and it tore people from shelters and fortified homes.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r11.anchor: أي مجاوز للحد من شدة عصفها وعظمة قصفها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r12.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r12.claim: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and Ibn ʿAbbās report that winds and rain normally descend measured by an angel, except the Flood and ʿĀd’s wind, which God let overwhelm their keepers.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r12.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طالب وابن عباس

BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r13.claim: The wind’s unprecedented force shows that God created and directed it by choice, not nature, as punishment for those who denied His rule and the Resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p121/r13.anchor: كانت بقدرته واختياره قهرا لمن طعن في ملكه

DURR-FULL:v8p264/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p264/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p264/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that God aided with the east wind and destroyed ʿĀd with the west; a ring-sized wind order overwhelmed its keepers, swept herders and camps into the city, and crushed its people, who had mistaken it for rain.
DURR-FULL:v8p264/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: نصرت بالصبا وأهلكت عاد بالدبور قال: ما أمر الخزان أن يرسلوا على عاد إلا مثل موضع الخاتم

DURR-FULL:v8p264/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p264/r3.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p264/r3.claim: ʿIkrima explains ṣarṣar as cold and ʿātiya as the wind's transgression against its keepers.
DURR-FULL:v8p264/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة رضي الله عنه قال: الصرصر الباردة {عاتية} قال: حيث عتت على خزانها

DURR-FULL:v8p264/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p264/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p264/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {عاتية} قال: شديدة

DURR-FULL:v8p264/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p264/r6.speaker: قبيصة بن ذؤيب
DURR-FULL:v8p264/r6.claim: Qubayṣa ibn Dhūʾayb says wind-keepers normally know every wind's measure, but ʿĀd's wind escaped their knowledge in God's anger, so it was called defiant; Noah's water similarly became overflowing.
DURR-FULL:v8p264/r6.anchor: من طريق ابن شهاب عن قبيصة بن ذؤيب قال: ما يخرج من الريح شيء إلا عليها خزان يعلمون قدرها وعددها

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3369#4/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3369#4/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3369#4/r1.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports the Prophet’s account that only a ring-sized portion of the wind was unleashed on ʿĀd; it lifted desert people, livestock, and property into the air, then cast them onto the town, whose residents mistook it for rain.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3369#4/r1.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p346/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p346/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p346/r5.claim: The fierce wind's description as ʿātiya means it exceeded its proper measure and defied its keepers, who could not control it; the wind was discussed at 41:16.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p346/r5.anchor: والريح الصرصر قد فسرناها في حم السجد 16 والعاتية التي جاوزت المقدار وجاء في التفسير أنها عتت على خزانها يومئذ فلم يكن لهم عليها سبيل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r14.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r14.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r14.claim: ʿAli reports that water and wind were normally measured by angels; on Noah's day water was released beyond its reservoirs and overflowed, while on ʿĀd's day the wind was released and exceeded its keepers' control.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p209/r14.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب قال: لم تنزل قطرة من ماء إلا بكيل على يدي ملك، فلما كان يوم نوح أذن للماء دون الخزان

JISHUMI:v10p7056/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7056/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7056/r5.claim: Thamūd were destroyed by the blast and ʿĀd by the wind; the account begins and ends with “day.”
JISHUMI:v10p7056/r5.anchor: ومنها: أن ثمود أهلكت بالصيحة، وعاد بالريح، وابتداؤها كان باليوم، والختم باليوم.

MUQATIL:69:5-12/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:69:5-12/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:69:5-12/r2.claim: For 'Ad, أهلكوا means that they were punished.
MUQATIL:69:5-12/r2.anchor: يعني عذبوا { بريح صرصر } يعني باردة

MUQATIL:69:5-12/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:69:5-12/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:69:5-12/r3.anchor: يعني عذبوا { بريح صرصر } يعني باردة

MUQATIL:69:5-12/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:69:5-12/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:69:5-12/r4.claim: The wind was intensely violent, exceeding its stores without pity or mercy.
MUQATIL:69:5-12/r4.anchor: { عاتية } [آية: 6] شديدة عتت على خزائنها بغير رأفة ولا رحمة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#2/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#2/r1.claim: The Prophet said that he was supported by the east wind and Aad were destroyed by the west wind.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#2/r1.anchor: لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم نصرت بالصبا واهلكت عاد بالدبور

NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#2/r2.claim: “صرصر” may mean intensely loud, from “الصرة” (a cry), or intensely cold, from “الصر”; repeated cold burns by its severity.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#2/r2.anchor: شديدة الصوت من الصرة الصيحة أبو باردة من الصر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#2/r3.claim: The wind was either fiercely violent or beyond its keepers' control by God's permission, as wrath against His enemies.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p274#2/r3.anchor: شديدة العصف أو عتت على خزانها فلم يضبطوها بإذن الله غضبا على أعدا الله

QURTUBI-FULL:69:6-7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:6-7/r1.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:69:6-7/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak says ṣarṣar is cold wind whose cold burns like fire, deriving the word from ṣarr, cold.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:6-7/r1.anchor: أي باردة تحرق ببردها كإحراق النار مأخوذ من الصر وهو البرد قاله الضحاك.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:6-7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:6-7/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:69:6-7/r2.claim: Another explanation says ṣarṣar means a wind of intense sound.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:6-7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:6-7/r3.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:69:6-7/r3.claim: Mujahid glosses ṣarṣar as intensely scorching wind.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:6-7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:6-7/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:69:6-7/r4.claim: The wind was uncontrollable by its keepers and too powerful for them to restrain; it raged with God's anger.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:6-7/r4.anchor: أي عتت على خزانها فلم تطعهم، ولم يطيقوها من شدة هبوبها غضبت لغضب الله.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:6-7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:6-7/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:69:6-7/r5.claim: Another explanation says the wind defied and overpowered the people of Aad.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:6-7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:6-7/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:69:6-7/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas reports from the Prophet that winds and water drops are normally measured, except the wind on Aad's day and water on Noah's day: each overwhelmed its angelic keepers. The report quotes 69:11 and 69:6.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:6-7/r6.anchor: روى سفيان الثوري عن موسى بن المسيب عن شهر بن حوشب عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:
